text: THELEELA.NS is the spotlight: it’s a hotel stock with 35.4% 1-year CAGR and only -16.3% max drawdown, but revenue YoY is down -17.1% in the latest quarter and operating margins have fallen from 48.7% to 31.5% over the last two quarters. That margin compression is a red flag—earnings surprise was +34.8% on Oct 14, yet the stock dropped -0.8% the next day, suggesting the beat was already priced in or concerns about forward guidance outweighed the surprise. For a 10x goal, this isn’t a compounder; it’s a mean-reversion play at best. In India, with Rs 10,000, you could buy ~12 shares at today’s Rs 833.15, but the 0.38% delivery charge and 20% short-term tax eat into any quick gain. Better to wait for a clearer trend or look at higher-beta names if you’re swinging for 10x.
